text:
alex: Heads up — we just saw a sudden p99 latency bump for hosted text-gen. p95 from ~220ms -> 470ms, p99 ~1.6s. No increase in 5xx. Spike started ~2199989950 and persists. Anyone on p99 hunt?
ops-bot: Deploy note: kernel-selector v2.3.1 rollout at 2199989900 (5% -> 100% ongoing).
maria: On it. Looking at queue depth across pools — eu-west-1-gpu-a shows backlog growth and a lot of small batches (batch size median dropped from 16 -> 3).
rohan: I pulled kernel logs. kernel-selector is frequently choosing the "fallback-int8" kernel for sequences > 1024 due to a sequence-length heuristic misclassifying request shapes. Fallback has higher per-token overhead. fallback_count +58% on impacted nodes.
sam: Profiler snapshot (trimmed):
```
flame: runtime_kernel_execute -> fallback_int8_conv -> memory_copy -> schedule_wait
hotspots: kernel_launch (42%), memcpy (18%), coalesce_wait (15%)
```
This aligns with smaller batches causing worse kernel efficiency + memcpy overhead.
irene: Also seeing KV cache churn: eviction rate up 4x on the same hosts. Possible noisy tenant generated many long context requests that broke caching locality.
alex: So combo: rollout path -> selector picks fallback -> batches shrink -> KV cache thrash -> higher latency. Agree?
maria: Yes. Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel-selector to v2.3.0, 2) force pin kernel to preferred path for hosted API, 3) temporarily increase coalescing window to favor larger batches, 4) route noisy tenant to dedicated pool. Which do we prefer for fast rollback?
rohan: Fastest is rollback 2.3.1 -> 2.3.0 (control plane). I've prepared rollback playbook. But pinning kernel via runtime config is also quick and more surgical.
sam: We should also throttle the sampling that triggered selector to misclassify — selector uses a sampled sequence-length histogram (sample_rate=0.02). On high variance traffic this sample is noisy. Lowering to 0.005 or using median-based bucketing would reduce flip-flop.
irene: For immediate relief, route 10% of traffic from eu-west-1-gpu-a to other healthy pools and increase coalesce window from 5ms -> 12ms. That should raise median batch size and reduce memcpy overhead.
alex: Action list: rohan rollback patch queued now, maria run routing shift + coalesce bump, sam prepare selector sampling patch and kernel pin config, irene add noisy-tenant filters. I'll coordinate with infra exec.
maria: Routing shift applied to 10% via traffic-weight override. Coalesce window increased in config -> will propagate in 30s.
rohan: Rollback started at 2199990060, monitoring logs.
sam: I'm uploading a short heap/kvstats dump to the incident channel. Early signs: kvcache hit rate climbs when batch size > 8, so routing + coalesce is promising.
ops-bot: Alert suppressed: p99 trend decreasing (new p99 ~980ms).
alex: Good. Keep monitoring for 15m. After stability window, let's do a controlled canary of a selector patch (sam's sampling change + cap on fallback ratio). Nobody wants a full 2.3.1 re-roll without that.
rohan: Agreed. I'll prepare a canary that pins fallback ratio < 5% and uses median bucket logic.
ire ne: small note: need to update rollout docs so selector rollbacks include coalesce/kv-checklist. We've lost that cross-config dependency once.
alex: Noted — will add to action items. Thanks all, marking triage in-progress. :thumbsup:
